::: {#sol-six-nine}

Suppose there are integers $m$ and $n$ with $6m + 9n = 1$.
Then

$$
\ba
1
&= 6m + 9n
&& \text{(the assumption, read from right to left)}
\\&= 3 (2m + 3n),
&& \text{(distributive law, read from right to left)}
\ea
$$

and $2m + 3n$ is an integer (@rem-integer-closure),
so $3 \mid 1$ (@def-divides).

But $3 \nmid 1$:
since $3 \cd 0 = 0 < 1 < 3 = 3 \cd 1$,
no integer $c$ has $3c = 1$.
So $3 \mid 1$ and $3 \nmid 1$, which is impossible.
The assumption must be false,
so there are no integers $m$ and $n$ with $6m + 9n = 1$.

:::
